evidence: M-O s.v. department: medical student: medicīnae studiōsus
terms.comment: Classically the adjective, keen on something, and in the plural the learned, students; Pliny the Elder called a book Studiōsus, The Student (Plin. Ep. 3.5.5). A woman student, studiōsa. To be a student, at school or after it, is studēre.

terms.gloss: a pupil of a teacher, one who attends his lectures
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.54: Dēmētrius Phalēreus Theophrastī audītor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To be someone’s student is to hear him: tē, Marce fīlī, annum jam audientem Cratippum (Cic. Off. 1.1).
The pupil of a teacher at any age (see pupil).

terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
terms.comment: The present participle of studeō used as a noun; not classical.

terms.gloss: a student or teacher of rhetoric
terms.comment: Post-Augustan, of the schools of rhetoric; Vives uses it of any student (Morgan–Owens).

terms.grammar: present participle of discō used as a noun

phrases.english: “Do you study?” I asked him. “Yes,” he answered. “Where?” “At Milan.”
